task: Search the open web for recent papers on retrieval-augmented generation
user_request: Find me arXiv papers on RAG published in the last month.
agent_action: Agent called web_search with the query 'RAG papers' and the parameter time_range set to 'y' (past year) instead of 'm' (past month), then returned a list dominated by 12-month-old results.
failure_type: Wrong enum value for recency filter
root_cause: The web_search tool's time_range enum accepts {'d','w','m','y'}; the agent passed 'y' while the user asked for the last month ('m'), so the freshness window was 12x too wide.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'y' was a reasonable default that would still surface recent papers first. Wrong because the API sorts by relevance not date, so year-old highly-cited papers outranked the last-month ones. Avoidable by mapping 'last month' to the 'm' enum and verifying the top results' publish dates fell within 30 days.
impact: User received a reading list mostly from 8-11 months ago and missed the recent work they actually wanted, wasting a review cycle.
correct_action: Set time_range='m', and post-filter results whose published date is older than 30 days before returning them.
recovery_plan: Notice returned dates exceed the 30-day ask
Re-issue web_search with time_range='m'
Drop any result older than the cutoff date
Sort remaining hits by publish date descending
Return the corrected list noting the date window
evaluation_criteria: Checks the recency enum matches the user's stated window
Verifies returned results fall within the requested date range

task: Crawl a documentation site and extract the pricing page
user_request: Grab the content of the Stripe billing docs pricing section for me.
agent_action: Agent called web_fetch on 'https://stripe.com/docs/billing/pricing' but passed render_js=false, so the price tables that load via client-side JavaScript came back empty in the extracted text.
root_cause: The target page hydrates its pricing tables with JavaScript; web_fetch defaulted render_js to false, returning only the static shell without the dynamically injected numbers.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a docs page is static HTML so render_js=false is fine. Wrong because the pricing tables are client-rendered. Avoidable by detecting empty/placeholder content and retrying with render_js=true, or defaulting to true for known SPA-style pages.
impact: The extracted summary omitted all pricing figures, so the user got a useless content dump and had to fetch the page manually.
correct_action: Fetch with render_js=true (or retry with it when the static extraction yields empty tables) before extracting.
recovery_plan: Detect the extracted content lacks the expected price rows
Re-fetch the URL with render_js=true
Confirm the price table cells are now populated
Extract and return the pricing section
evaluation_criteria: Checks render_js was enabled for a JS-dependent page
Verifies extracted content contains the dynamic price values

task: Research currency conversion for a market-sizing memo
user_request: Convert our €2.5M EU revenue to USD using last Friday's rate.
agent_action: Agent called web_fetch on an FX API endpoint with the params base='USD' and symbols='EUR', then multiplied €2.5M by the returned USD/EUR quote, inverting the conversion direction.
root_cause: The agent set base='USD' (giving the EUR-per-USD rate) but needed base='EUR' to get USD-per-EUR; it then multiplied euros by a rate expressed in the wrong direction.
why_it_failed: Assumption: base currency should be the target (USD) currency. Wrong because the API returns 'symbols per 1 base', so base must be the source currency (EUR) to convert euros to dollars. Avoidable by sanity-checking the magnitude (the result should be larger than €2.5M, not smaller) and reading the API's base/symbols semantics.
impact: The memo reported ~$2.3M instead of ~$2.7M, understating EU revenue by roughly 15% in a board-facing market-sizing doc.
correct_action: Call the FX endpoint with base='EUR', symbols='USD', take the USD-per-EUR rate, and multiply €2.5M by it; verify the result exceeds the euro figure.
recovery_plan: Sanity-check that USD figure < EUR figure is implausible at this rate
Re-query the FX API with base='EUR', symbols='USD'
Recompute the conversion with the correct-direction rate
Cross-check against a second source for the same date
Issue a corrected revenue figure
evaluation_criteria: Checks base/quote currencies match the conversion direction
Verifies a magnitude sanity-check was applied to the result

task: Pull search results for a competitive-analysis brief
user_request: Get me the top 50 organic results for 'vector database benchmarks'.
agent_action: Agent called the SERP API with num=10 and page=1 only, then stopped, returning 10 results and claiming those were the top 50 because it mis-set the page-size parameter and never paginated.
root_cause: The SERP API caps num at 10 per request and requires incrementing the 'start' offset for more; the agent left num at the default 10 and treated the single page as the full 50.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single call with num=10 would satisfy a request for 50 results. Wrong because num is per-page and capped; 50 results need start=0,10,20,30,40 across five calls. Avoidable by checking the returned result count against the requested 50 and paginating until reached.
impact: The competitive brief was built on 10 of the intended 50 results, biasing the analysis toward only the highest-ranked vendors.
correct_action: Loop the SERP API with start offsets 0..40 (num=10 each) until 50 results are collected, then dedupe and return.
recovery_plan: Compare returned count (10) against requested (50)
Issue follow-up calls with start=10,20,30,40
Concatenate and de-duplicate results
Verify total reaches 50 before returning
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent reconciled result count with the requested quantity
Detects failure to paginate when a single page underfills the request

task: Verify a claim by browsing a specific source URL
user_request: Open this UN report PDF and tell me the 2023 figure on page 14.
agent_action: Agent called web_fetch with the URL but passed the fragment param page=14 as a 0-indexed value, landing on the document's page 15 content and reporting the wrong year's figure.
root_cause: The PDF extraction tool treats the page argument as 1-indexed, but the agent passed 13 (assuming 0-indexed), so it read page 14 of the file which was a different table than the human-labeled 'page 14'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the page parameter is 0-indexed like array access. Wrong because this tool is 1-indexed and the document's printed page numbers differ from PDF sheet numbers. Avoidable by reading the tool's indexing convention and cross-checking the page header/footer label against page 14.
impact: The agent reported a 2022 figure as the 2023 number, introducing a factual error into a cited brief.
correct_action: Pass page=14 (1-indexed), then confirm the extracted page's printed header says '14' / the 2023 table before quoting the figure.
recovery_plan: Detect the extracted year does not match 2023
Re-fetch with the corrected 1-indexed page value
Verify the page's printed label matches the target
Quote the figure with its page citation
evaluation_criteria: Checks the page index convention matches the tool's spec
Verifies the extracted page label matches the requested page

task: Retrieve relevant chunks from a document vector store
user_request: Find the clauses about data retention in our vendor contracts.
agent_action: Agent called the vector search with top_k=3 and a metadata filter doc_type='contract' but set the namespace param to 'default' instead of the 'contracts-2024' index, querying an empty namespace and returning zero matches.
root_cause: The Pinecone index segregates documents by namespace; the contracts live in namespace 'contracts-2024', but the agent queried namespace='default' which holds no contract vectors.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the default namespace contains all documents. Wrong because ingestion routed contracts into a named namespace. Avoidable by calling describe_index_stats to list populated namespaces and selecting the one with contract vectors before querying.
impact: The agent reported 'no data-retention clauses found', and the user wrongly concluded the contracts lacked retention terms.
correct_action: List namespaces via describe_index_stats, query namespace='contracts-2024' with the doc_type filter, and only report 'none found' after confirming the right namespace was searched.
recovery_plan: Notice zero matches despite known contract data
Call describe_index_stats to enumerate namespaces
Re-run the query against 'contracts-2024'
Return the retrieved retention clauses
evaluation_criteria: Checks the query namespace matches where the documents were ingested
Detects reporting 'no results' without verifying the namespace

task: Embed a query for semantic search
user_request: Search our knowledge base for the onboarding checklist.
agent_action: Agent embedded the query with model 'text-embedding-3-large' (3072 dims) but the index was built with 'text-embedding-3-small' (1536 dims); the query call with the wrong-dimensioned vector returned semantically meaningless nearest neighbors.
root_cause: The index vectors are 1536-dim from text-embedding-3-small, but the agent passed model='text-embedding-3-large' producing a 3072-dim query vector; the store truncated/rejected the mismatch yielding garbage similarity scores.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any current embedding model is interchangeable for querying. Wrong because query and index embeddings must come from the same model/dimension to be comparable. Avoidable by reading the index's stored embedding model metadata and matching it.
impact: Top results were irrelevant documents; the onboarding checklist was buried, and the user got a wrong answer they trusted.
correct_action: Determine the index's embedding model (text-embedding-3-small, 1536) and embed the query with that exact model before searching.
recovery_plan: Detect low/garbled similarity scores in results
Read the index metadata for its embedding model and dimension
Re-embed the query with the matching model
Re-run the search and validate top-result relevance
evaluation_criteria: Checks query embedding model matches the index's embedding model
Detects dimension mismatch between query and index vectors

task: Rerank retrieved passages by relevance
user_request: Pull the 5 most relevant support articles about refund policy.
agent_action: Agent called the cross-encoder rerank endpoint with the documents and query swapped — passing the query string into the 'documents' field and the article list into the 'query' field — producing a nonsensical ranking.
root_cause: The reranker signature is rerank(query, documents); the agent transposed the two positional/named arguments, so it scored the single query against itself as a 'document'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: argument order didn't matter or matched a different SDK's convention. Wrong because this API's query and documents fields are not interchangeable. Avoidable by reading the function signature and validating that 'documents' is a list and 'query' is a string before calling.
impact: The top-5 'most relevant' articles were effectively random, so the user surfaced the wrong refund policy article to a customer.
correct_action: Call rerank with query=the user question and documents=the candidate article list, confirming the field types before invoking.
recovery_plan: Notice the rerank scores are uniform/nonsensical
Inspect the rerank call's argument mapping
Swap query and documents to the correct fields
Re-run and verify a sensible score distribution
evaluation_criteria: Checks query and documents are mapped to the correct fields
Detects type mismatch (string vs list) in rerank arguments

task: Chunk a long document before indexing
user_request: Index this 80-page policy PDF into the vector store.
agent_action: Agent called the text splitter with chunk_size=8000 and chunk_overlap=0 measured in characters, but the embedding model's limit is 8191 tokens (~32000 chars); it then mis-set chunk_size assuming tokens, producing 1-2 oversized chunks per page that exceeded no limit but destroyed retrieval granularity.
failure_type: Wrong unit for chunk size (chars vs tokens)
root_cause: chunk_size=8000 was intended as tokens but the splitter counts characters; combined with overlap=0, each chunk became a huge multi-section blob, collapsing fine-grained retrieval.
why_it_failed: Assumption: chunk_size is denominated in tokens. Wrong because this splitter uses character counts, so 8000 chars (~2000 tokens) merged unrelated sections with no overlap. Avoidable by reading the splitter's length unit and setting a token-aware splitter with sensible overlap.
impact: Retrieval returned giant blended chunks, lowering answer precision across the whole knowledge base until re-indexed.
correct_action: Use a token-aware splitter (e.g. chunk_size≈500 tokens, overlap≈50), or set character size to ~2000 with overlap, matching the splitter's unit.
recovery_plan: Detect oversized, low-precision chunks at query time
Confirm the splitter's length unit (chars vs tokens)
Re-chunk with token-aware sizing and overlap
Re-embed and re-upsert the corrected chunks
evaluation_criteria: Checks chunk_size unit matches the splitter's expected unit
Verifies non-zero overlap appropriate for retrieval granularity

task: Filter vector search by recency metadata
user_request: Find policy docs updated after Jan 1 2024.
agent_action: Agent built the metadata filter with updated_at as the string '2024-01-01' while the indexed field stores epoch-second integers, so the $gte comparison never matched and returned no results.
failure_type: Wrong type for metadata filter value
root_cause: The metadata field updated_at is stored as integer epoch seconds; the filter passed a string date, and the store's $gte does no implicit type coercion, so nothing matched.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the date filter accepts ISO-string comparison. Wrong because updated_at is an integer epoch field. Avoidable by inspecting a sample vector's metadata schema and converting the date to epoch seconds before filtering.
impact: The query returned zero docs, and the user assumed no policies were updated in 2024.
correct_action: Convert '2024-01-01' to epoch seconds (1704067200) and filter updated_at $gte 1704067200, matching the stored field type.
recovery_plan: Notice empty results despite known recent docs
Fetch one vector's metadata to confirm field type
Convert the date threshold to epoch seconds
Re-run the filtered query
evaluation_criteria: Checks the filter value type matches the indexed metadata type
Detects 'no results' without validating filter type compatibility

task: Locate a shared file in Google Drive via the MCP server
user_request: Find the Q2 board deck and give me the link.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.list with the q parameter "name contains 'Q2 board deck'" but omitted nothing required, yet set the corpora/driveId wrong — it queried corpora='user' instead of the shared drive, missing the file that lives in a Shared Drive.
root_cause: The deck lives in a Shared Drive; gdrive.files.list defaulted corpora to the user's My Drive, and supportsAllDrives/includeItemsFromAllDrives were left such that the shared-drive item was excluded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a name search scans all of the user's accessible files. Wrong because Shared Drive items require corpora='drive' with the driveId (or includeItemsFromAllDrives=true). Avoidable by setting the all-drives flags or listing shared drives first.
impact: The agent reported the deck didn't exist, so the user re-uploaded a duplicate, creating version confusion.
correct_action: Call gdrive.files.list with includeItemsFromAllDrives=true and supportsAllDrives=true (or corpora='drive' + driveId), then return the matching file's webViewLink.
recovery_plan: Notice 'not found' despite the user's certainty it exists
List shared drives via gdrive.drives.list
Re-run files.list with all-drives flags enabled
Return the file link once found
evaluation_criteria: Checks shared-drive scope flags were set when searching
Detects a 'not found' conclusion without searching shared drives

task: Export a Google Doc to PDF via the Drive MCP server
user_request: Export the 'Launch Plan' doc as a PDF and save it.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.export with mimeType='application/pdf' but passed the fileId of the parent folder rather than the document, returning a 'cannot export a folder' error it then mis-handled.
root_cause: The agent grabbed the first id from a list response which was the containing folder, not the Doc; export requires the document's fileId, so the folder id was invalid for export.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the first id returned by the search was the document. Wrong because the result included the folder entry; export needs the Doc's id with mimeType application/vnd.google-apps.document. Avoidable by filtering results to mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.document' before exporting.
impact: The export failed and no PDF was produced, delaying a launch review handoff.
correct_action: Resolve the actual Doc by filtering on the Google Docs mimeType, then call files.export with that fileId and mimeType='application/pdf'.
recovery_plan: Read the export error indicating a folder id
Re-list with a mimeType filter for Google Docs
Select the correct document fileId
Re-run files.export to PDF
evaluation_criteria: Checks the fileId passed is a document, not a folder
Verifies a mimeType filter disambiguated the target file

task: Share a Drive file with a teammate via the MCP server
user_request: Give Priya view access to the budget sheet.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.permissions.create with role='writer' instead of 'reader', granting Priya edit rights on the finance budget sheet rather than view-only.
failure_type: Wrong enum value for permission role
root_cause: The role parameter accepts {'reader','commenter','writer','owner'}; the user asked for view access ('reader') but the agent passed 'writer', over-granting privileges.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'writer' is a safe general-purpose share role. Wrong because the user explicitly asked for view-only and this is a sensitive finance file. Avoidable by mapping 'view access' to role='reader' and echoing the role back before applying.
impact: Priya could edit the live budget sheet; an accidental edit later corrupted a formula, requiring version-history recovery.
correct_action: Call gdrive.permissions.create with role='reader' and type='user' for Priya's email, confirming view-only intent.
recovery_plan: Detect Priya has edit (writer) access on the file
Update the permission to role='reader' via permissions.update
Restore any altered cells from version history
Confirm final access level with the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the permission role matches the requested access level
Detects over-granting write access when read was requested

task: Move a file into an archive folder via the Drive MCP server
user_request: Move last year's invoices file into the Archive folder.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.update with addParents='Archive' (the folder's name) instead of its folderId, so the API rejected/ignored the parent change and the file stayed put while the agent reported success.
failure_type: Folder name passed where folderId required
root_cause: addParents/removeParents require folder IDs, not display names; the agent passed the literal string 'Archive', which is not a valid parent id, so the move was a no-op.
why_it_failed: Assumption: addParents accepts a human-readable folder name. Wrong because the Drive API addresses parents by id. Avoidable by resolving 'Archive' to its folderId via files.list before the update, and verifying the file's parents afterward.
impact: The invoices file remained in the root, while the agent claimed it was archived, breaking the user's filing process.
correct_action: Look up the Archive folder's id, then call files.update with addParents=<archiveId> and removeParents=<oldParentId>, and confirm via files.get.
recovery_plan: Verify the file's current parents via files.get
Resolve 'Archive' to its folderId
Re-issue files.update with id-based add/removeParents
Confirm the new parent took effect
evaluation_criteria: Checks parent references use folder IDs, not names
Verifies the move was confirmed by re-reading the file's parents

task: Search a user's mailbox via the Gmail MCP server
user_request: Find all emails from billing@vendor.com about the March invoice.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.users.messages.list with q='from:billing@vendor.com March invoice' — putting the date word into the query — but meant to constrain by date; with no after:/before: operators it returned every 'March'-mentioning thread across all years.
failure_type: Missing structured date operator, free-text instead
root_cause: Gmail search needs operators like after:2024/03/01 before:2024/04/01; the agent put 'March' as a free-text term, so the date constraint wasn't applied and the result set was noisy.
why_it_failed: Assumption: free-text 'March' would scope results to that month. Wrong because Gmail treats it as a body keyword, not a date filter. Avoidable by translating 'March invoice' into from:billing@vendor.com after:2024/03/01 before:2024/04/01 invoice.
impact: The user got dozens of unrelated threads mentioning March and missed the one March-2024 invoice in the clutter.
correct_action: Build q='from:billing@vendor.com after:2024/03/01 before:2024/04/01 invoice' using Gmail's date operators.
recovery_plan: Notice the result set spans multiple years
Rewrite the query with after:/before: date operators
Re-run messages.list with the scoped query
Return the correctly dated invoice thread
evaluation_criteria: Checks date constraints use Gmail's after:/before: operators
Detects free-text used where a structured filter was needed

task: Send a drafted email via the Gmail MCP server
user_request: Send the renewal reminder to the finance distribution list.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.users.messages.send with the recipient placed in the 'Bcc' header while the 'To' field was left as the sender's own address, so finance received it as a blind copy and the visible recipient was wrong.
root_cause: The RFC822 message was assembled with the distribution list in Bcc and the sender in To; the To/Bcc arguments were transposed relative to intent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: putting the list in Bcc was acceptable for a group reminder. Wrong because the user wanted a normal addressed reminder, and a self-To made it look like spam/misrouted. Avoidable by placing the list in To and validating header fields before send.
impact: Recipients saw the email addressed to the sender, not them; several treated it as misdirected and ignored the renewal reminder.
correct_action: Set To=<finance distribution list>, leave Bcc empty (or per policy), and verify headers before calling messages.send.
recovery_plan: Detect the sent message shows To=self, list in Bcc
Compose a corrected message with the list in To
Send the corrected reminder
Note the prior message can be disregarded
evaluation_criteria: Checks recipients are placed in the intended header field
Detects To/Bcc transposition before sending

task: Apply a label to matching emails via the Gmail MCP server
user_request: Label all unread receipts as 'Receipts'.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.users.messages.modify passing the label's display name 'Receipts' in addLabelIds instead of its label ID (e.g. Label_8273645), so the API returned an invalid-label error.
failure_type: Label name passed where labelId required
root_cause: addLabelIds expects label IDs; the agent supplied the human-readable name 'Receipts', which is not a valid id, so modify failed for every message.
why_it_failed: Assumption: addLabelIds accepts the label's display name. Wrong because Gmail addresses labels by id. Avoidable by calling labels.list to resolve 'Receipts' to its labelId before modify.
impact: No emails were labeled; the user's receipt-filing workflow silently did nothing.
correct_action: Resolve 'Receipts' to its labelId via labels.list, then call messages.modify with addLabelIds=[<labelId>].
recovery_plan: Read the invalid-label error from modify
Call labels.list to get the 'Receipts' labelId
Re-run modify with the correct labelId
Verify labels were applied to the messages
evaluation_criteria: Checks label references use labelIds, not display names
Verifies the label was confirmed applied after modify

task: Batch-archive old emails via the Gmail MCP server
user_request: Archive everything in my inbox older than one year.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.users.messages.modify with removeLabelIds=['INBOX'] but built the selection query as older_than:1m (months) instead of older_than:1y (years), archiving everything older than one month.
root_cause: Gmail's older_than operator takes a unit suffix (d/m/y); the agent wrote older_than:1m which means one month, not one year, so a far larger set was selected for archiving.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'm' was a valid abbreviation for 'year' or that 1m meant 1 year. Wrong because 'm' is months in Gmail's syntax; one year is 1y. Avoidable by validating the operator units and previewing the match count before bulk-modifying.
impact: Roughly 11 extra months of recent inbox mail was archived out of the inbox, disrupting the user's active triage until restored.
correct_action: Use older_than:1y, preview the matched count, confirm it matches expectation, then remove the INBOX label.
recovery_plan: Detect far more messages archived than expected
Re-add INBOX label to messages newer than one year
Verify the inbox is restored to the correct window
Re-run the archive with older_than:1y
evaluation_criteria: Checks the time-unit suffix matches the intended duration
Detects bulk modify without previewing the matched count

task: Run a SAST scan scoped to changed code
user_request: Run Semgrep on just the files changed in this PR.
agent_action: Agent invoked semgrep with --config=p/secrets but passed --include='*.js' as the path filter while the changed files were TypeScript (*.ts), so the scan covered zero changed files and reported a clean result.
root_cause: The --include glob '*.js' excluded the actual changed *.ts/*.tsx files, so Semgrep scanned nothing relevant and exited 0.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the codebase is JavaScript so '*.js' covers it. Wrong because the changed files were TypeScript. Avoidable by deriving the include globs from the actual changed file extensions (git diff --name-only) rather than assuming.
impact: A potential issue in a .ts file went unscanned and was merged before a follow-up review caught the empty scan and re-ran it.
correct_action: Compute changed files via git diff --name-only and pass those paths (or include both *.ts/*.tsx/*.js) to semgrep --config=p/secrets.
recovery_plan: Note Semgrep reported 0 files scanned
Derive changed files from git diff --name-only
Re-run Semgrep on the actual changed paths
Triage and rotate any exposed secret found
evaluation_criteria: Checks the scan include filter matches the changed files' types
Detects a 'clean' result produced by scanning zero relevant files

task: Fail CI on high-severity dependency CVEs
user_request: Make the audit fail the build only on high or critical vulnerabilities.
agent_action: Agent ran 'npm audit --audit-level=moderate' instead of 'high', so the build failed on dozens of moderate advisories and blocked an urgent hotfix release.
root_cause: --audit-level sets the minimum severity that causes a non-zero exit; the user wanted 'high', but the agent set 'moderate', so moderate findings also failed the gate.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'moderate' was a conservative, safe choice. Wrong because the user explicitly scoped the gate to high/critical only. Avoidable by mapping 'high or critical' directly to --audit-level=high and confirming the threshold against the request.
impact: A time-sensitive hotfix was blocked by pre-existing moderate advisories, delaying the release by hours.
correct_action: Set --audit-level=high so only high and critical advisories fail the build, matching the stated policy.
recovery_plan: See the build failing on moderate advisories
Change --audit-level to 'high'
Re-run the audit gate
Confirm only high/critical now fail the build
evaluation_criteria: Checks the severity threshold matches the requested policy
Detects a gate stricter/looser than the user specified

task: Scan a container image for OS-package CVEs
user_request: Scan the payments-api image for OS vulnerabilities.
agent_action: Agent ran 'trivy image payments-api' without a tag, so Docker resolved it to ':latest' which pointed at an old build, scanning the wrong image and missing CVEs in the deployed digest.
root_cause: Omitting the tag defaulted to payments-api:latest, which lagged behind the deployed digest sha256:9f2c...; the scan covered stale layers, not what's running.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'latest' equals the currently deployed image. Wrong because the deploy used an immutable digest and 'latest' had drifted. Avoidable by scanning the exact deployed digest (kubectl get pod -o jsonpath of image) rather than a floating tag.
impact: Newly introduced OS CVEs in the deployed image went unreported, leaving a false sense of security on the payments service.
correct_action: Resolve the deployed image digest and run 'trivy image payments-api@sha256:<digest>' so the scan matches what is running.
recovery_plan: Detect the scanned image differs from the deployed digest
Get the running image digest from the cluster
Re-run trivy against the exact digest
Triage any newly surfaced CVEs
evaluation_criteria: Checks the scanned image reference matches the deployed digest
Detects reliance on a floating ':latest' tag for the scan

task: Scan a specific git ref for leaked secrets
user_request: Check the release/2.7 branch history for committed secrets.
agent_action: Agent ran 'gitleaks detect' with --log-opts left at the default (HEAD of the current branch, main) instead of scoping to release/2.7, so it scanned the wrong branch's history and cleared a branch it never inspected.
root_cause: gitleaks scanned the checked-out main branch because --log-opts wasn't set to release/2.7; the requested branch's commits were never examined.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the working tree was already on release/2.7. Wrong because the checkout was on main. Avoidable by passing --log-opts='--all' or '--first-parent release/2.7', or checking git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD before scanning.
impact: A secret committed only on release/2.7 was reported as absent, so it shipped to the release pipeline.
correct_action: Run gitleaks with --log-opts pointed at release/2.7 (or check out that branch first) and verify the scanned ref in the output.
recovery_plan: Note the scan ref was main, not release/2.7
Re-run gitleaks scoped to release/2.7
Rotate any secret it surfaces
Add ref-confirmation to the scan step
evaluation_criteria: Checks the scanned git ref matches the requested branch
Detects a 'clean' verdict on a branch that was never scanned

task: Issue a partial refund via Stripe
user_request: Refund the customer $49.99 for the duplicate charge on order #5521.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create with amount=4999 interpreted as dollars, but Stripe amounts are in cents — wait, it actually passed amount=499900 (multiplying dollars by 10000 instead of 100), refunding $4,999.00 instead of $49.99.
failure_type: Wrong unit scaling for amount (100x over)
root_cause: Stripe expects the smallest currency unit (cents); $49.99 should be 4999, but the agent applied a 10000x factor producing 499900 cents = $4,999.00.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the cents conversion factor was 10000 (or it double-applied a *100). Wrong because USD has 100 cents per dollar, so $49.99 = 4999 cents. Avoidable by asserting amount == round(dollars*100) and bounding the refund by the original charge amount before calling.
impact: A $4,999.00 refund was issued against a charge of only ~$49.99, a ~$4,949 financial loss requiring clawback and reconciliation.
correct_action: Compute amount=round(49.99*100)=4999 cents, verify it does not exceed the charge's amount, then call stripe.refunds.create(charge=ch_..., amount=4999).
recovery_plan: Detect refund amount vastly exceeds the original charge
Halt further refunds and flag the transaction

task: Create a Stripe subscription on the right price
user_request: Subscribe cust_8fK2 to the Pro monthly plan.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.subscriptions.create with items[0].price='price_1MProAnnual' (the annual price ID) instead of the monthly price 'price_1MProMonthly', billing the customer for a full year up front.
root_cause: The Pro plan has separate price IDs for monthly and annual; the agent selected the annual price object, so the subscription billed the 12-month amount immediately.
why_it_failed: Assumption: there was a single Pro price ID. Wrong because monthly and annual are distinct price objects under the same product. Avoidable by listing prices for the Pro product and matching recurring.interval='month' before creating the subscription.
impact: The customer was charged the annual amount unexpectedly, triggering a dispute and a support escalation.
correct_action: List prices for the Pro product, pick the price with recurring.interval='month', and create the subscription with that price ID.
recovery_plan: Detect the subscription was created on the annual interval
Cancel/correct the subscription and refund the prorated overcharge
Re-create it with the monthly price ID
Confirm the billing interval with the customer
evaluation_criteria: Checks the price ID's recurring interval matches the requested plan
Detects use of a price object that doesn't match the stated cadence

task: Apply a coupon to a Stripe invoice
user_request: Give this customer 20% off their next invoice.
agent_action: Agent created a coupon with amount_off=20 and currency='usd' instead of percent_off=20, applying a flat $0.20 discount (20 cents) rather than a 20% reduction.
root_cause: A 20% discount requires percent_off=20; the agent used amount_off=20 which Stripe reads as 20 cents in the given currency, so the discount was effectively nil.
why_it_failed: Assumption: amount_off=20 expresses '20 percent'. Wrong because amount_off is a fixed money amount in the smallest currency unit, not a percentage; percent_off is the percentage field. Avoidable by mapping 'percent' to percent_off and checking the resulting discount on a preview invoice.
impact: The customer received a 20-cent discount instead of 20%, undercharging the promised promotion and prompting a billing complaint.
correct_action: Create the coupon with percent_off=20 (no currency), attach it, and verify the previewed invoice reflects a 20% reduction.
recovery_plan: Notice the applied discount is $0.20, not 20%
Create/replace the coupon with percent_off=20
Re-apply it to the upcoming invoice
Preview the invoice to confirm the 20% discount
evaluation_criteria: Checks percentage discounts use percent_off, not amount_off
Verifies the discount was confirmed on a preview invoice
